name: Hong Kong Codes of Practice (Buildings Department)
description: A thin pack for Hong Kong (alpha 9 track C23): it extends the legacy British Standards pack bs8110 and sets what the Hong Kong Codes of Practice change. Wind by the Code of Practice on Wind Effects in Hong Kong 2019: the design pressure by height from the code's reference pressures (one profile for the territory, a generic method of speedFactors), the topography factor Sq on the pressure, Sθ and the size and dynamic factor taken 1.0 (rigid buildings; the dynamic response is not covered). Concrete by the Code of Practice for Structural Use of Concrete 2013 where it differs from BS 8110: γm 1.15 for the bars, the stress block depth 0.9 x / 0.8 x / 0.72 x and the neutral axis limit 0.5 d / 0.4 d / 0.33 d by grade, εcu above C60, Ec = 3.46 √fcu + 3.21 kN/mm², vc with fcu up to 80 and the maximum shear stress 0.8 √fcu up to 7 N/mm². Imposed loads of the Code of Practice for Dead and Imposed Loads 2011 for dwellings, offices and roofs. Steel: the HK Code of Practice for the Structural Use of Steel 2011 follows BS 5950-1 for the members SAEngine designs; its own values are not set, the parent's BS 5950-1:2000 values apply (named BS 5950-1 in the report). Earthquake: not covered (zone 0, no earthquake cases; Hong Kong's seismic provisions are not included). Load combinations, cover, the other loads and the rest: BS 8110 / BS 6399 (the parent), then BNBC 2020. Every value is listed in VERIFY.md: the wind pressures and the imposed loads are to be checked against the printed codes before design.

basis.general: HK Code of Practice on Wind Effects 2019 and Code of Practice for Dead and Imposed Loads 2011; load combinations of BS 8110-1 Table 2.1 (the HK concrete code's Table 2.1 is the same form); no seismic loading
basis.concrete: HK Code of Practice for Structural Use of Concrete 2013 where it differs from BS 8110-1:1997; the rest by BS 8110 (parent pack bs8110), torsion, flat slabs, walls and footings from BNBC 2020 until covered
basis.steel: BS 5950-1:2000 members (the HK Code of Practice for the Structural Use of Steel 2011 values not set)
